{"id": "37:143/q17", "question": "What inward reading is drawn from the glorification?", "turns_on": "The sources offer distinct inward applications of the whale and glorification.", "positions": [{"id": "37:143/q17/p1", "position": "In crisis Jonah lost attachment to self and all else, remaining in God's oneness through glorification.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī says this inward state illuminates his rescue."}, {"id": "37:143/q17/p2", "position": "The lower self is like a whale engulfing the heart; constant remembrance brings rescue.", "reasons": "Bursawī makes the whale a figure for the lower self, adding that turning to God in ease brings help in hardship and good works support the person who falls."}]}

Bursevī includes any speech; Ṭabāṭabāʾ rejects unsupported restrictions."}, {"id": "39:18/q03/p3", "position": "They are Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr and Salmān, pre-Islamic monotheists.", "reasons": "Ibn Zayd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd report that the three avoided idols, affirmed God's oneness, and followed the best teaching or reason available without scripture or prophet."}, {"id": "39:18/q03/p4", "position": "They are Abū Bakr's early converts: ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿīd and Saʿd.", "reasons": "ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās includes Abū Bakr as first believer; other reports list the six, who heard his profession and believed."}, {"id": "39:18/q03/p5", "position": "They include an Anṣārī who freed seven slaves after hearing of Hell's seven gates.", "reasons": "Jābir reports that after 15:44 he freed one for each gate and received this verse as good news."}]}
{"id": "39:18/q04", "question": "Why describe the listeners explicitly rather than use a pronoun?", "turns_on": "The rhetorical force assigned to the explicit description.", "positions": [{"id": "39:18/q04/p1", "position": "It identifies the promised servants and highlights attentive discernment.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī links wholehearted devotion to listening and following; al-Bayḍāwī stresses discerning truth, al-Nasafī the combination of repentance and judgment, Abū Ḥayyān careful hearing."}, {"id": "39:18/q04/p2", "position": "It singles out people of exceptional standing.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī calls them chosen people of high aspiration; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the fresh sentence draws attention to their deserving divine care."}]}
{"id": "39:18/q05", "question": "What speech do they hear?", "turns_on": "Whether al-qawl is scripture, a broader field of utterance, or a historically specific hearing.", "positions": [{"id": "39:18/q05/p1", "position": "The Qur'an or God's Book.", "reasons": "Muqātil, Muqātil and Yaḥyā as reported by al-Māwardī, al-Baghawī and al-Wāḥidī identify the saying as scripture; Abū Ḥayyān reports this with Qur'anic pardon and forbearance."}, {"id": "39:18/q05/p2", "position": "Speech broadly, including guidance and error from any speaker.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya praises weighing all kinds. Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the definite noun generic, including Qur'an, prophetic instruction and fabrication. Al-Biqāʿī urges hearing every speaker. Bursevī includes God, angels, humans, Satan and the self; human speech varies in truth and goodness."}, {"id": "39:18/q05/p3", "position": "The Qur'an alongside other speech.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj and many later interpreters use this comparison; Ṭabāṭabāʾ rejects making it an exclusive restriction."}, {"id": "39:18/q05/p4", "position": "God's commands and competing lawful courses, sometimes also prophetic instruction.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj and al-Kashshāf compare pardon and retaliation; al-Qāshānī includes duties, recommendations, strictness and dispensations from God or others; al-Qurṭubī includes the Messenger's statements and clearer rulings."}, {"id": "39:18/q05/p5", "position": "Earlier communities' sayings heard by people without divine scripture.", "reasons": "Ibn Zayd is reported by al-Māwardī."}, {"id": "39:18/q05/p6", "position": "Speech connected with action, whose best form surely guides and counsels.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾ infers the action connection from 'they follow'."}]}
{"id": "39:18/q06", "question": "How do they listen?", "turns_on": "Whether their listening is characterized chiefly as receptivity or critical comparison.", "positions": [{"id": "39:18/q06/p1", "position": "Attentively and openly, seeking truth before judgment.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī contrasts wholehearted hearing with stubborn dismissal; Ṭabāṭabāʾ says they fear missing truth and reflect instead of obeying desire; Iṣlāḥī contrasts careful hearing with aggression; Abū Ḥayyān stresses attentive listening."}, {"id": "39:18/q06/p2", "position": "They hear rival claims for rational comparison.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī says hearing is common to all while reason distinguishes the soundest; Kur'an Yolu reports his appeal to rational proof."}]}
{"id": "39:18/q07", "question": "What does أَحْسَنَهُ mean as a comparison?", "turns_on": "Whether the form grades good alternatives or serves as simple or emphatic praise.", "positions": [{"id": "39:18/q07/p1", "position": "A truly better, more fitting option among good ones.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī contrasts permissible good with more fitting best; Ṭabāṭabāʾ says love of goodness moves one from good to better; al-Ṭabrisī stresses worthiness of acceptance and action."}, {"id": "39:18/q07/p2", "position": "Simply good.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī reports this sense of 'best'."}, {"id": "39:18/q07/p3", "position": "An intensified praise, without ranking two good sayings.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr cites Joseph's 'prison is dearer' at 12:33."}]}
